title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: There is no $\varepsilon > 0$ for which there is an algorithm for testing isomorphism of maps of unrestricted genus in time $O(n^{2-\varepsilon})$.
context_text: A map is an embedding of a connected graph in a closed compact surface such that every face is homeomorphic to an open disc; an isomorphism of maps is a bijection preserving the vertex-edge-face incidences, and $n$ denotes the size of the map (e.g. its number of darts). In the simultaneous conjugation problem, given permutations $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_d$ and $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_d$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, each family generating a transitive group, one seeks $\gamma$ with $\gamma\alpha_i\gamma^{-1}=\beta_i$ for all $i$; map isomorphism is the special case $d=2$ with $\alpha_1,\beta_1$ involutions acting on the darts. Map isomorphism is solvable in quadratic time, and in linear time on the sphere (Hopcroft and Wong) and for bounded genus; the authors compute generators of the automorphism group of a map of genus $g$ in time $f(g)n$. For unrestricted genus, simultaneous conjugation is solvable in $O(dn^2)$ (known since the 1970s) and in $O(n^2\log d/\log n+dn\log n)$ (recent), giving $O(n^2/\log n)$ for map isomorphism and automorphism, which is not considered truly subquadratic. This motivates the conjecture that no $O(n^{2-\varepsilon})$ algorithm exists.

title: Open subproblem: conditional superlinear lower bound
statement_text: An interesting open subproblem is to prove a conditional ``truly superlinear'' lower bound for any of the problems of testing isomorphism of maps of unrestricted genus, computing the automorphism group of such maps, and simultaneous conjugation of permutations.
context_text: A map is an embedding of a connected graph in a closed compact surface such that every face is homeomorphic to an open disc; an isomorphism of maps is a bijection preserving the vertex-edge-face incidences, and $n$ denotes the size of the map (e.g. its number of darts). In the simultaneous conjugation problem, given permutations $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_d$ and $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_d$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, each family generating a transitive group, one seeks $\gamma$ with $\gamma\alpha_i\gamma^{-1}=\beta_i$ for all $i$; map isomorphism is the special case $d=2$ with $\alpha_1,\beta_1$ involutions acting on the darts. Map isomorphism is solvable in quadratic time, and in linear time on the sphere (Hopcroft and Wong) and for bounded genus; the authors compute generators of the automorphism group of a map of genus $g$ in time $f(g)n$. For unrestricted genus, simultaneous conjugation is solvable in $O(dn^2)$ (known since the 1970s) and in $O(n^2\log d/\log n+dn\log n)$ (recent), giving $O(n^2/\log n)$ for map isomorphism and automorphism, which is not considered truly subquadratic. The authors conjecture that map isomorphism for unrestricted genus has no $O(n^{2-\varepsilon})$ algorithm. As partial progress towards lower bounds, the communication complexity of simultaneous conjugation is $\Omega(dn\log n)$ for $d>1$, and in the decision tree model the search version has an $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound; a conditional lower bound of the form $n^{1+\varepsilon}$ remains open.
